Slots.maps_to: encounter/_slot_order (proposed shared mechanism id) -- kaiser_crab.py's default Encounter.create_monsters never sets Creature.slot_name
Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: KaiserCrabBoss.cs:29 declares Slots=["crusher","rocket"], and GenerateMonsters (KaiserCrabBoss.cs:49-56) tags Crusher with "crusher" and Rocket with "rocket", in that order. `KAISER_CRAB_BOSS = Encounter(id="kaiser_crab_boss", monster_classes=[Crusher, Rocket])` (kaiser_crab.py:159-162) uses the base `Encounter.create_monsters` with no `slots=`/`monster_slots=` override, so no `Creature.slot_name` is ever assigned for either arm. EXECUTED WITNESS: same game-wide `SlotName` consumer grep as filed for decimillipede in this batch (`grep -rln SlotName src/` -- 16 files, none of them Crusher.cs or Rocket.cs) -- confirms neither arm's own move logic (back-attack bonus, rage-on-partner-death, targeting) reads `Creature.SlotName`; those mechanics key off CLASS identity (Crusher IS the left arm, Rocket IS the right arm) and live combat state (which side the player is currently targeting), not the slot string. Cross-checked the sim side: `kaiser_crab.py`'s `Crusher`/`Rocket` never read `self.slot_name` either -- `BackAttackLeftPower`/`BackAttackRightPower`/`CrabRagePower`/`SurroundedPower` are applied unconditionally at construction, keyed by which Python class was instantiated. Dormant today: `SortEnemiesBySlotName` (CombatState.cs:495-501) would be a no-op even in the game, because GenerateMonsters' own return order (Crusher@0, Rocket@1) already equals the Slots row order (crusher@0, rocket@1) -- there is nothing to reorder. Filed under the same shared mechanism id as decimillipede's Slots gap (`encounter/_slot_order`) since both are instances of the same family: an encounter declares a Slots row purely for a placement its own roster order already satisfies, and the sim omits the row + assignment entirely rather than modeling (and no-op-ing) it explicitly.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk); run_env.py:1074 boss-identity vocabulary reads Encounter.monster_classes directly
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: KaiserCrabBoss.cs:33-37 declares exactly {Crusher, Rocket} -- the same 2 classes GenerateMonsters always returns. Same consumer census as the rest of the batch for the C# property itself (UI/debug only: dev-console unlock list, bestiary ratio). Separately confirmed the ONE place the sim genuinely needs a boss-identity-preview vocabulary that is NOT the global class walk: `run_env.py:1074`'s observation-encoder boss-identity block iterates `room_set.next_boss_encounter.monster_classes` directly (the dataclass field, not a global scan) to populate the known-boss-ahead observation. For `KAISER_CRAB_BOSS`, `monster_classes=[Crusher, Rocket]` is populated (this unit does not override `create_monsters`, unlike the units that leave the field an unused empty list), so this consumer is correctly served. Cost: none observed for this unit; noted for the controller that any Hive/other-act BOSS encounter whose sim counterpart DOES override `create_monsters` and leaves `monster_classes` empty would starve this specific consumer -- worth a pool-wide sweep across all `boss_keys` entries in every act (none of Hive's three bosses in this batch hit it; kaiser_crab is the only boss in my unit list).
